observations: Only an intact owned Author5 managed News post in a single-post context is eligible. Anonymous drafts, ordinary posts, wrong owner/category/source and archive contexts receive no head or schema correction.
An owned draft stage additionally requires actual current user5 with sgnews_publish. Public canonical posts require publish status. The exact configured site remains https://sggroup.jp.

The existing AIOSEO graph is modified in place only when exactly one Article, BlogPosting or NewsArticle node exists. It becomes NewsArticle with free access, approved headline/language/URL and SG Group Organization author/publisher; zero or multiple article nodes remain unchanged.

The wp_head output buffer removes canonical and ja/en/x-default alternate link tokens and emits one own canonical and reciprocal shared-slug links. Comments and raw script/style/title/textarea content are preserved. Unclosed raw text/comments, changed post context and mismatched nested buffers cancel correction.
The source diff introduces no capability grant, authentication change, new remote route, source sanitizer change, publication lifecycle change, database write, cron or outbound HTTP action.

Controlled-first execution is internally bound to one revision, event, baseline date, full JA/EN payload, current Python/connector code and Author5 runtime. It consumes fresh action/quota receipts, requires four real prepublication gates and all eight article checks, reuses freshly verified known stages and preserves durable publication/reconciliation/public QA.

Partial first-pair recovery verifies the already-public canonical source and identity before publishing the missing peer. Ordinary execute/run_pending continue to require all six gates and an unpaused runtime; controlled-first success does not change pause or promote postpublication gates.
limitations: Offline tests do not verify the installed WordPress, MySQL, active theme or installed AIOSEO implementation. Production frontend HTML/schema, actual metadata roundtrip and public URL QA remain required.
This review did not install 0.1.1, grant any role/capability, send WordPress requests, publish an article or enable an hourly schedule.
The installed source must match this exact PHP SHA before using its runtime proofs; earlier 0.1.0 source approval does not certify the new code.
Structured operator receipts are not cryptographic execution attestation; private files and exact digests bind the recorded evidence to the reviewed execution.
